card.summary: H.R. 6719, titled the James T. Woods Act, is a federal bill that expands legal frameworks regarding the online exploitation and coercion of children. It directs the U.S. Sentencing Commission to update guidelines for child sexual abuse material offenses, creates new criminal offenses for online coercion of minors to commit harm or self-harm, and criminalizes threats to distribute child sexual abuse material to intimidate, coerce, extort, or cause substantial emotional distress.

summary: The ECCHO Act establishes a federal criminal framework to address the online coercion of minors. It creates new federal offenses for intentionally coercing minors to commit suicide, kill people or certain animals, commit serious bodily injury, or commit arson, doxxing, or swatting. It requires electronic communication and remote computing service providers to report instances of online coercion to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children via the CyberTipline, facilitates federal prosecution of offenders, and expands court protections for certain child victims and witnesses.

affected_groups.effect: Protected from online coercion to commit harmful acts, and granted expanded courtroom and privacy protections if they are victims or witnesses.
Subject to federal criminal prosecution, fines, and prison terms up to life depending on the severity of the coerced act.

affected_groups.group: Electronic communication and remote computing service providers

key_provisions: Makes it a federal crime to intentionally coerce a minor using interstate commerce or communications to commit suicide, kill individuals or specific animals, or inflict serious physical harm.
Criminalizes the intentional coercion of a minor to commit arson, doxxing, swatting, or making false reports of active threats.
Sets penalties including fines and imprisonment for any term of years or up to life for suicide or homicide coercion, and up to 30 years for other specified coerced acts.
Requires electronic communication and remote computing service providers to report online coercion instances to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children via the CyberTipline.
Facilitates the federal prosecution of offenses committed by child exploitation enterprises and minors in certain circumstances.
Extends court testimony privacy and other protections to child victims and witnesses of mental injury or negligent treatment.
